name: scientific_visualization

knowledge_assets.title: Publication figure integrity and accessibility
knowledge_assets.purpose: Review deceptive encodings, missing-data handling, accessibility cues, and static or interactive delivery boundaries.

knowledge_assets.title: Color, contrast, and palette selection
knowledge_assets.purpose: Choose palettes by data semantics and audit contrast, grayscale separation, normalization, and redundant encodings.

knowledge_assets.title: Publisher and journal figure snapshots
knowledge_assets.purpose: Plan figure dimensions, formats, resolution, fonts, and submission-stage checks using dated publisher snapshots.

knowledge_assets.title: Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly examples
knowledge_assets.purpose: Provide current plotting and export patterns for scoped styles, uncertainty, normalization, and static fallbacks.

knowledge_assets.title: Visualization source registry
knowledge_assets.purpose: Track official URLs, access dates, versions, and research basis for visualization guidance.

knowledge_assets.title: Nature-style starting point
knowledge_assets.purpose: Use as a dated visual starting point only; it is not a journal-compliance certification.

knowledge_assets.title: Presentation style starting point
knowledge_assets.purpose: Provide larger projected-display defaults while keeping scientific semantics and explicit export settings under agent control.

knowledge_assets.title: Publication style starting point
knowledge_assets.purpose: Provide a restrained print-oriented style baseline; final journal settings must still be checked live.

knowledge_assets.title: Publisher planning profiles
knowledge_assets.purpose: Supply machine-readable dated screening defaults for export planning without claiming compliance.

description: Scientific visualization is a cross-domain visualization primitive for truthful, accessible, publication-ready figures. Use it for figure design, multi-panel layouts, uncertainty and missing-data displays, color and contrast review, image metadata validation, and export planning.
capabilities: Choose visual encodings that preserve scientific meaning.
Plan uncertainty, missing data, transformations, and accessibility cues.
Specify Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, raster, vector, and journal export constraints.
requirements: Source data or image provenance and transformation notes.
Target medium and export requirements when known.
Appropriate plotting or export tooling for execution.
